scenes.headline: How a Blender add-on makes a rigged character
scenes.sub: A mesh model, a rigger, and a server doing the heavy work
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sinew! This add-on turns a prompt into a character that can walk, and most of the work happens off screen.

scenes.text: Blender holds the controls. A ComfyUI server runs the models that draw the image, build the mesh and predict the skeleton.
scenes.mark: A ComfyUI server runs the models
scenes.say: Blender is the control panel. A separate server runs the models that draw, build and rig.

steps.say: A prompt makes a gallery of preview images, and you pick one.
TRELLIS dot two builds a mesh from the picked image.
SkinTokens then predicts the skeleton and the skin weights for that mesh.
Views painted around the model are projected on as texture, and the result exports.

scenes.title: Twisting a forearm
scenes.say: When a clip is retargeted, the add-on splits each rotation into a swing and a twist.

parts.note: how much twist can be read
parts.say: The twist part has a length.
It shrinks as the swing grows, and only vanishes at a half turn.

steps.say: The rigger is a separate paper. It compresses skin weights into a few discrete tokens.
A language model then writes the skeleton and those tokens as one sequence.

scenes.label: of VRAM quoted for SDXL texturing, not for the mesh or the rig
scenes.note: no figure found for those stages
scenes.say: The eight gigabytes you may have seen is for the texture stage only.

scenes.text: Blender is the front end. Models on a server make the character; only the retargeting maths runs without a GPU.
scenes.mark: only the retargeting maths runs without a GPU
scenes.say: Blender is the front end. Only the retargeting maths runs without a graphics card.
Pick an image, build the mesh, predict the rig, then retarget in Blender.
